title: Coefficient-unit purity and reduction of finite diagonal orientations
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a smooth separated morphism of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Write $\ell=u\varpi_E^e$ with $u$ a unit and $e\geq1$, and put $R_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n=A_{E,en}$ for $n\geq1$. Use the ordinary derived categories of strict varying-coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], their uniform constructible finite-Tor full subcategories $\mathcal C_T=\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$ [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], and ordinary derived tensor products [def-weil-derived-tensor]. Twists are [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and $F_\bullet=Rf_{!,\bullet}\dashv G_\bullet=f^!_\bullet$ with finite units, counits and evaluations is [det-sp-tower-gluing]. Put $\mathbf1_{\bullet,T}=(R_{n,T})_n$ and $\omega_\bullet=G_\bullet\mathbf1_{\bullet,Y}$, so $\omega_n=f^!_{R_n}R_{n,Y}$; pullback means levelwise finite derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

Let $a_n:R_{n,X}(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_n$ be the inverse of the finite diagonal isomorphism [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] at index $en$. Let $\gamma_{f,R_n}$ denote the specified inverse-diagonal-orientation/tensor-transpose map [def-pur-smooth-purity-map, def-pur-co-smoothness], using the compactification projection map [def-exchange-projection]. Under the tensor-unit identifications,
$$\theta_{f,R_{n,Y}}=1_{\omega_n},\qquad a_n=\gamma_{f,R_n}(R_{n,Y}).$$
The orientation and purity comparison defined over $R_n$ by [det-sp-finite-general-ring] agree with these maps at index $en$. For every $1\leq m\leq n$, under canonical Tate reduction [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor],
$$c_{n,m}(R_{n,Y})\circ(a_n)_{R_m}=a_m.$$
Here $(-)_{R_m}=-\otimes^L_{R_n}R_m$ and $c_{n,m}$ is the coefficient comparison [det-sp-reduction-compatibilities]. This is the compatibility for the actual reduction maps of $\omega_\bullet$: these reduction maps are $c_{n,m}(R_{n,Y})$ under the finite evaluations of $G_\bullet$.

source.place: (1), finite diagonal orientations, coefficient-unit tensor map and quotient compatibility; retained proof steps 1-2

proof.text: Since $\ell=u\varpi_E^e$ with $u$ invertible, $(\ell^n)=(\varpi_E^{en})$. Thus the quotient $R_n$ with its constant sheaf is canonically $A_{E,en}$. Apply [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] at the positive index $en$ to obtain $\Pi_n:\omega_n\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{n,X}(d)[2d]$ and set $a_n=\Pi_n^{-1}$. All its scheme hypotheses hold: $f$ is smooth, separated, of finite type and pure dimension $d$, over the stipulated $k$. The coefficient unit $R_{n,Y}$ is a constant finite free rank-one sheaf, hence constructible, concentrated in degree zero and of Tor amplitude $[0,0]$: tensoring it with a degree-zero module sheaf gives that same sheaf. It is therefore an allowed input for the finite purity comparisons. For unit_tower_mem, identify evaluation of the actual sequence-site coefficient module with the regular finite coefficient module by evaluation_ring and transport along that ring equality. Exact evaluation commutes with the degree-zero single functor; levelComparison and the realization counit identify the inverse realization at every level with this single regular module. To prove its finite bounds, use the canonical intrinsic coefficient realization F. Its existing tensor comparison and essential surjectivity give F(1) isomorphic to 1: choose K with F(K) isomorphic to 1 and compose F(1) = F(1) tensor 1, the comparison with F(1 tensor K), and the left unitor of K. The fixed-scalar unit single is the comparison image of the constructible etale unit single. Exact homology comparison and the intrinsic constructibility equivalence transfer all its constructible cohomology sheaves. Its cohomology vanishes outside [0,0]; flatness of the unit gives fixed-scalar Tor amplitude [0,0], and intrinsic Tor-amplitude transport gives the same intrinsic bound. Finally transport these three properties across the finite-evaluation isomorphisms and use the single common pair of intervals [0,0] at every level. No normalization or invertibility of tower reductions enters membership.

For the specified ordinary-etale compact-support projection, apply the proved source-library theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.projectionMap_rightUnitality (WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.Etale.Derived.ProjectionFormula.Unit). It says that projection at the tensor unit, followed by the pullback-unit comparison and right unitor, is the right unitor of compact support. Thus its inverse has the corresponding unit normalization. This uses the actual projection map underlying [def-pur-co-smoothness], without separately reproving its proper and open factors.

Write F = Rf_!, G = f^!, U for the coefficient unit and omega = GU. Transpose the projection-unit identity of step 2 through F adjoint G. Adjunction.ext_of_comp_counit and map_projectionTensorMap_comp_counit identify the W-first tensor mate at U with omega tensor the pullback-unit hom followed by the right unitor. Naturality of braiding converts the coefficient-first smoothTensorDualityMap to the left unitor after the inverse pullback-unit comparison. Finally whisker exchange moves the inverse orientation past that comparison, and left-unitor naturality proves gamma(U) = alpha.inv. The private generic categorical helpers in the Lean module implement these equalities; no additional purity statement is assumed. For the comparison-origin single-complex unit, naturality of this tensor mate transports the identity along smoothPurityUnitIso. This gives smoothPurityEtaleTheta equal to the pullback-unit comparison followed by the left unitor. The specification of diagonalDualizingObject writes it as diagonalDualizingComparison followed by the comparison functor applied to its ordinary orientation. Expand smoothPurityTensorMapInPresentation and smoothPurityTheta, move that inverse orientation through the pullback and tensor comparison using naturality, cancel diagonalDualizingComparison.inv followed by .hom, and use left-unitor naturality. The remaining arrows are exactly the displayed sourceUnitIso followed by diagonalDualizingObject.inv, proving canonical_purity_at_unit without an additional purity assumption.

The ring $R_n$ is finite and killed by $\ell^n$. Clause (2) of [det-sp-finite-general-ring] identifies its scalar-extended orientation with the orientation obtained by the direct diagonal and deformation construction with $R_n$ coefficients, which is $\Pi_n$ at the index $en$. Taking inverses gives precisely $a_n$. Clause (3) defines the general-ring purity map by this inverse orientation followed by the tensor transpose of the inverse compact-support projection and the same counit. These are the factors in step 3, so the general-ring and $A_{E,en}$ purity maps agree (also for general allowed $K$). No arbitrary isomorphism between the two dualizing objects is being selected. For uniformizer_purity_agreement, apply the already proved ordinaryGammaCoefficient from ReductionCompatibilities to the coefficient equivalence, the two displayed orientations and uniformizer_orientation_agreement. This general tensor-mate formula holds on every ordinary input K, so the stated bounded constructible finite-Tor hypothesis is not needed for this final formal substitution. Its tensor source is definitionally the published diagonalTwistEtale ordered line. The orientation agreement and the remaining tower clauses retain their recorded proofs to be formalized.

Apply normalizedOrientation_scalar from lem-sp-finite-normalized-orientation-scalar to the actual quotient RingHom.ulift (SpTowerCalculus.quotient l E hmn), N=l^(n+1) and M=l^(m+1). Positivity follows from primality of l and M dividing N from m≤n. finiteGeneralRingPrimeSetting supplies N invertible on Y and X and M invertible on X. The two input normalization predicates and t are exactly the inputs of that generic theorem. Its complete factorization and square-pasting proof gives the displayed inverse-orientation equality without changing a coefficient map or root comparison.

Apply lem-sp-coefficient-unit-tower-normalized to the inverse section realization of the actual coefficient unit. The supplied identification of whole towers gives an isomorphism from K to this inverse realization, by composing the realization unit with the inverse functor applied to the identification. Naturality of the canonical reduction expresses its component on K as the component on that unit conjugated by the scalar-extended n-th evaluation and the inverse m-th evaluation of this isomorphism. Thus the actual input reduction is invertible. Levels.reduction from det-sp-tower-gluing identifies scalar extension of the n-th exceptional evaluation comparison followed by the coefficient mate and the finite right adjoint of the input reduction with the actual exceptional-output reduction followed by the m-th comparison. Postcompose this equality with the finite right adjoint of the inverse input reduction. Functoriality and the hom-inverse identity cancel the last two factors. This is exactly unit_tower_reduction, including the specified proof of input invertibility and actual coefficientMate.
